'''Wolfgang Helfrich''' (26 March 1932 – 28 September 2025) was a German physicist and inventor who made contributions to twisted-nematic [[liquid crystal]] technology, which is used to produce a variety of modern [[Liquid-crystal display|LCD electronic displays]],<ref name="Lipo">{{Cite journal |last=Lipowsky |first=R. |date=1994 |editor-last=Schwuger |editor-first=M. J. |editor2-last=Haegel |editor2-first=F. H. |title=Wolfgang Ostwald Prize 1993 awarded to Wolfgang Helfrich |url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/BFb0115699 |journal=Surfactants and Colloids in the Environment |language=en |location=Darmstadt |publisher=Steinkopff |pages=3–4 |doi=10.1007/BFb0115699 |isbn=978-3-7985-1668-7|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=11 October 2025 |author=Freie Universität Berlin |date=11 October 2025 |language=de |publisher=Der Tagesspiegel |title=Wolfgang Helfrich |type=† 28 September 2025 in Berlin |url=https://trauer.tagesspiegel.de/traueranzeige/wolfgang-helfrich |website=trauer.tagesspiegel.de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and in the field of biomembranes.

== Career ==
Helfrich studied physics in Munich, Göttingen, and Tübingen.{{Citation needed|date=September 2020}} Helfrich joined [[RCA Corporation|RCA]] in 1967, became interested in [[Charles-Victor Mauguin]]'s [[Twisted nematic field effect#TN-effect|twisted structure]], and thought it might be used to create an [[electronic display]]. However, RCA showed little interest, because they felt that any effect that used two [[polarizer]]s would also have a large amount of light absorption, requiring it to be brightly lit.{{Citation needed|date=September 2020}}

In 1970, Helfrich left RCA and joined the Central Research Laboratories of [[Hoffmann-LaRoche]] in Switzerland, where he teamed up with Swiss physicist [[Martin Schadt]], a solid-state physicist.<ref name="Japan">{{cite book | last1=Kawamoto | first1=Hirohisa | title=2012 Third IEEE HISTory of ELectro-technology CONference (HISTELCON) | chapter=The history of liquid-crystal display and its industry | date=28 March 2013 | pages=1–6 | doi=10.1109/HISTELCON.2012.6487587 | isbn=978-1-4673-3079-4 }}</ref> Schadt built a sample with electrodes and a twisted version of a liquid-crystal material called PEBAB (p-ethoxybenzylidene-p'-aminobenzonitrile), which Helfrich had reported in prior studies at RCA, as part of their guest-host experiments.

From 1973 until his retirement in 1997, Helfrich worked for [[Free University of Berlin]].<ref>[https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/3805321/Biophysics_Prize_Awarded_to_W__Helfrich_and_C__Bustamante.html Biophysics Prize Awarded to W. Helfrich and C. Bustamante]</ref> In 1973, Wolfgang Helfrich published the first complete description of the [[Elasticity of cell membranes|bending energy of membranes]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Helfrich |first=W |date=1973-12-01 |title=Elastic Properties of Lipid Bilayers: Theory and Possible Experiments |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209/html |journal=Zeitschrift für Naturforschung C |language=en |volume=28 |issue=11-12 |pages=693–703 |doi=10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209 |issn=1865-7125|doi-access=free }}</ref> In 1978, he set up the first theory of the steric repulsion of membranes caused by shape fluctuations.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Helfrich |first=W. |date=1978-03-01 |title=Steric Interaction of Fluid Membranes in Multilayer Systems |url=https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/zna-1978-0308/html |journal=Zeitschrift für Naturforschung A |language=en |volume=33 |issue=3 |pages=305–315 |doi=10.1515/zna-1978-0308 |issn=1865-7109|doi-access=free }}</ref> In the 1970s and following decades, Wolfgang Helfrich made numerous theoretical and experimental contributions to membrane physics, in particular on vesicle shapes, membrane shape fluctuations, and the effect of electric fields on vesicles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wolfgang Helfrich {{!}} biomembrane-days-2012.mpikg.mpg.de |url=https://biomembrane-days-2012.mpikg.mpg.de/node/5/index.html |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=biomembrane-days-2012.mpikg.mpg.de}}</ref>

Helfrich lived in [[Berlin]] where he died on 28 September 2025, at the age of 93.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=11 October 2025 |date=11 October 2025 |language=de |publisher=Der Tagesspiegel |title=Hans Wolfgang Helfrich |url=https://trauer.tagesspiegel.de/traueranzeige/hans-wolfgang-helfrich |website=trauer.tagesspiegel.de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

== Works ==
* ''Untersuchungen an raumladungsbeschränkten Defektelektronenströmen in Anthrazen'' - Munich 1961
* ''Raumladungsbeschränkte Ströme in Anthrazen als Mittel zur Bestimmung der Beweglichkeit von Defektelektronen'' - Munich 1961
* ''Space-charge-limited and volume-controlled currents in organic solid'' - Munich 1967
*''Elastic properties of lipid bilayers : theory and possible experiments'', Zeitschrift für Naturforschung C, vol. 28, 1973
*''Deformation of lipid bilayer spheres by electric fields'', Zeitschrift für Naturforschung C, vol. 29, 1974.
*''Steric interactions of fluid membranes in multilayer systems'', Zeitschrift für Naturforschung 33a, 305, 1978.
*''Liquid Crystals of One- and Two-Dimensional Order'' - Berlin, Heidelberg : Springer Berlin Heidelberg, 1980
*''Elasticity and thermal undulations of fluid films of amphiphiles'', in: Liquides aux interfaces, École d'été de physique théorique, Les Houches, Session XLVIII, Université scientifique et médicale de Grenoble, Nato Advanced Study Institute, Institut national polytechnique de Grenoble, 1988, S. 209–238.

== Awards ==
* 1976 [[EPS Europhysics Prize]]
* 1993 [[Wolfgang Ostwald]] Prize<ref name="Lipo" />
* 2008 [[IEEE Jun-ichi Nishizawa Medal]]
* 2012 [[Sackler Prize]]
* 2012 [[Draper Prize|Charles Stark Draper Prize for Engineering]]
